questions.question: Why is tracking dollar cost more important than tracking token count for LLM observability?
choices: Tokens are harder to count than dollars
GPT-4 output tokens cost 6x more than input tokens — token count alone is misleading
Dollar amounts are easier to display in dashboards
Token counts are always zero due to API limitations
questions.explanation: Different models and token types have vastly different costs. GPT-4 output tokens ($0.006/1K) cost 6x more than input tokens ($0.003/1K). A call with 1000 output tokens costs 6x more than one with 1000 input tokens — token count alone doesn't tell you this.

questions.question: What information should each LLM trace record?
choices: Model used, prompt, response, token counts (input/output), latency, and computed cost
Only the timestamp and model name
Just the total cost rounded to the nearest dollar
questions.explanation: A complete trace records everything needed for debugging and cost analysis: which model was used, what was sent and received, how many tokens of each type, how long it took, and the computed dollar cost.

questions.question: Why is per-model cost breakdown essential in LLM observability?
choices: It makes the dashboard look more professional
Without it, you can't tell which model is driving costs or optimize accordingly
Each model requires a separate API key
Per-model tracking is required by OpenAI's terms of service
questions.explanation: If your total LLM cost is $45/month, you don't know where to optimize without per-model breakdown. Maybe GPT-4 is responsible for $40 of that — then you can route simpler tasks to GPT-3.5 to save.
